name: Operator edit-decision capture on the approvals rail
mechanism: The template's approval rail offers three decisions instead of two: approve, reject, and edit-then-send. The edited decision stores the operator's replacement text alongside the original draft, and the learning layer treats the operator's version, not the model's, as the positive exemplar, because an edit is the operator teaching. Rejected and pending outcomes are never captured; only satisfied outcomes become exemplars.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS already shipped the harvest logic (packages/core/src/exemplar.ts derives positive/negative exemplars and expects DecisionRecord.operatorText for edited decisions), but the input side does not exist: the approvals table (packages/db/src/schema.ts line 374) has no column for operator-corrected text, POST /api/approvals/:id/decide (apps/api/src/index.ts line 322) accepts only an optionKey, resolveApproval (packages/core/src/lifecycle.ts line 261) stores nothing structured, and the control-plane Approvals UI has no edit affordance. The richest learning signal is currently uncapturable.
improvement_sketch: Migration 0033: add decided_option_key text and operator_text text (nullable) to approvals. Extend the decide endpoint to accept an optional editedText body field; resolveApproval persists both and emits the option in the approval.resolved Relay payload. Control-plane Approvals route gains an edit-textarea flow (prefilled with proposedAction, submit = decide with editedText). Wire ExemplarSink.loadDecisions to map decided rows into DecisionRecord with decision='edited' when operator_text is present. No change to exemplar.ts itself.

name: One-pass self-critique against exemplars before a proposal is raised
mechanism: After drafting and before submission, a second cheap model pass compares the draft against stored exemplars (best prior outputs) and promoted principles, and returns either approve or exactly one revision. Two hard invariants: it runs at most once (a critique that loops until satisfied burns tokens forever), and it fails SAFE to the original draft on any malformed output, missing revision, or model error, because a human still reviews downstream so a flaky critique must never block or empty a good draft. The final draft is always non-empty when the original was.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's critic.ts is a peer-approval quorum: other agents vote on items already sitting in the approvals queue. There is no pre-submission self-revision step, so first-draft quality is what hits the operator inbox, which drags down approval rates — the very metric the autonomy ladder promotes on. The exemplar block (composeExemplarBlock) is injected as prompt context but nothing verifies the output against it.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/self-critique.ts: pure buildCritiquePrompt(draft, exemplars, principles), parseCritique(raw, original) with the keep-original fallback on every failure branch, and runSelfCritique with an injected model call (mirrors the sink pattern of objective.ts). Runner wires it in the propose path (apps/runner/src/execute.ts) just before the approval row is created, using the agent's tier model via the existing delegate plumbing; T-cheap agents critique on T-cheap. Emit a relay event (e.g. critique.revised) only when a revision was taken so the scorecard can correlate critique with approval rate.

name: Surgical fact-grounding corrector for outbound drafts
mechanism: A reviewer model receives the draft plus a CONTEXT block declared to be the only permitted facts, and returns a minimal list of find/replace/reason corrections instead of a rewrite (empty replace means delete the span, e.g. a hallucinated greeting name). Deterministic code then applies each correction only if its find-string occurs exactly once in the draft, so the edit is unambiguous and voice/structure cannot drift; a seam-cleanup pass fixes stranded spaces only when a deletion happened. Any unparseable review, failed call, empty draft, or unapplicable correction fails CLOSED to a needs_review verdict routed to human approval — the opposite failure polarity from the critique pass, because invented facts are a safety problem, not a quality problem.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's injection-guard scrubs INBOUND tool content; nothing verifies OUTBOUND content. Lead-pipeline agents (acqu-enrichment-scoring delegates drafting to Sonnet) and future outreach sends have no mechanical defense against hallucinated names, prices, or commitments in client-facing copy.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/grounding.ts: pure parseCorrections (strict shape validation, null on untrustworthy JSON), applyCorrections (exact-unique-substring apply, applied/unapplied split), cleanSeam, and reviewGrounding with injected model call and verdicts pass|corrected|needs_review. Runner exposes it inside the outbound-content path (wrap tool.delegate drafting or a dedicated tool.draft custom tool in apps/runner/src/custom-tools.ts): reviewer runs on a higher tier than the drafter (drafter T-cheap, reviewer T-work), needs_review verdicts force the propose/approval path regardless of autonomy level.

name: Layered oversend defense with a sends ledger
mechanism: Every send-class tool call is gated by a pure evaluator over layered state: shadow-mode kill switch (draft-only period after deploy), a hard requirement of an approved approval row for the run, a per-run send cap, and a per-recipient rolling 24h cap. The counts come from a dedicated sent-log ledger that the send tool itself writes after success, and every outbound POST carries a stable idempotency key (hash of run + path + payload) so the downstream system dedupes retries. The state read fails closed: if the ledger is unreadable you cannot prove the send is safe, so it is denied. The template's documented bug class is the reason the ledger is explicit: a 24h cap that reads a log nothing writes is a permanently dead defense with green tests.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS has autonomy gates (propose/execute_safe/execute_full), approval gates, and budget caps in hooks — but no send-rate machinery: no per-recipient rolling cap, no per-run send cap, no sent ledger, no idempotency keys on outbound webhook/email sends, no shadow-mode ramp for newly deployed agents. As the lead pipeline moves from scoring to actual outreach, unbounded duplicate sends to one recipient are the top operational risk.
improvement_sketch: Migration 0034: sent_log table (tenant_id, run_id, agent_id, recipient normalized, channel, idempotency_key unique, sent_at) with RLS. New packages/core/src/send-guard.ts: pure evaluateSendGate(state) returning allow plus the denying layer, isSendClass classifier over tool names/paths, buildIdempotencyKey. Wire into the runner's PreToolUse hook (apps/runner/src/hooks.ts) for send-class dispatches, failing closed when the ledger read throws; the send tool writes the ledger row post-success. Add tenants config knobs (per_run_send_cap, per_recipient_24h_cap, shadow_until) validated by tenant-config.ts.

name: Streaming budget kill-switch with cache-aware token accounting
mechanism: A per-run cost meter accumulates spend from every streamed SDK message's usage block — input, output, cache-read, and cache-write tokens each priced separately from a local per-model pricing table — and the run loop breaks the moment accumulated spend crosses the run budget, recording a distinct budget_exceeded stop reason. Cost enforcement is therefore mid-loop and per-message, not end-of-run.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS reads total_cost_usd and input/output tokens only from the final result message (apps/runner/src/execute.ts lines 353-357), and the BudgetTracker synthesizes one reserve+commit for the whole run (apps/runner/src/budget.ts comment says exactly this). A runaway loop is stopped only by maxTurns; cache read/write tokens are never accounted, so cached-heavy runs misreport spend through the OpenRouter gateway.
improvement_sketch: In the execute.ts stream loop, accumulate a running meter from each message's usage (including cache token fields) against the reserved cap and break with a capped status plus budget.capped relay emit when crossed mid-stream; extend RunResult and the runs table with cache token columns. Pricing table lives beside router/tier-models.ts keyed by fuel slug so the meter works for Hermes and Claude alike, used as fallback when the gateway omits cost.

name: Full per-message run transcript table
mechanism: Every message the SDK stream yields — assistant turns, tool_use inputs, tool_results, result — is persisted as one row (run id, message type, role, full payload) as it streams, giving a complete replayable transcript of the run. Run open/finish bookend rows carry task, context, budget, stop reason, turns, and spend, and a persistence failure degrades to a local id rather than killing the run.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS persists only assistant text slices (truncated to 2000 chars via postActivity in execute.ts line 350) and PostToolUse audit rows carrying toolName + inputHash — not the tool inputs/outputs themselves. There is no way to replay what a run actually saw and did, which hobbles forensics on anomaly-breaker trips and denies the eval loop its richest offline dataset.
improvement_sketch: Migration 0035: run_messages (tenant_id, run_id, seq, msg_type, role, payload jsonb, created_at) with RLS. In the execute.ts stream loop, insert each message non-fatally (log-and-continue on failure); honor doctrine rule 4 by storing file paths, not blobs, for large tool outputs (they already go to ctx.outputDir). Surface a transcript view on the control-plane run detail page.

name: Fail-closed triage front door for inbound-triggered runs
mechanism: Before any tool loop or drafting model runs, one small classifier call assigns the inbound to exactly one category from an injected set, where each category maps to ignore, escalate, or engage. The single invariant: a failed call, malformed JSON, or unknown category NEVER routes to the engage path — it always escalates to a human, because a classifier that fails open drafts autonomous replies to spam, hostile, and sensitive inbound. Cheap drops cost one tiny model call; sensitive content never reaches the expensive agent.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS agents are mostly cron-scheduled today, and the injection guard scrubs tool content, but there is no classification stage that decides whether a run should happen at all. A2A handoffs and any future inbound-triggered agents (inbox, webhook-driven) dispatch the full agent loop unconditionally, spending T-work tokens on noise and letting hostile inbound reach the drafting model.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/triage.ts: pure buildTriagePrompt(categories), parseTriage(raw, categories, fallbackId) where every failure branch returns action=escalate with failedClosed=true, and a runner with injected model call. Category sets live on the agent spec (agents are data), so each agent declares its own triage taxonomy. Wire into the runner predispatch path (apps/runner/src/predispatch.ts) for payload-carrying triggers, running on T-trivial/T-cheap; escalate creates an approval row instead of a run.

name: Scenario-scoped exemplar retrieval as a pull tool
mechanism: Besides injecting learned material into the prompt, the template exposes two read tools the agent calls at draft time: one fetches the most recent gold-standard exemplars filtered by the specific scenario being drafted, the other fetches active principles as the union of scenario-scoped rules plus always-included client-wide rules. Tool descriptions carry the doctrine ('imitate exemplars over written rules; principles are non-negotiable'), and the scenario filter keeps only relevant material in context.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's exemplar loop is push-only: composeExemplarBlock builds one bounded 1600-char block per agent injected into the bundle, mixing all task labels. An agent handling several task types gets diluted or truncated exemplars, and cannot ask for more relevant ones for the task at hand even though Exemplar records already carry taskLabel.
improvement_sketch: Add a tool.exemplars.fetch custom tool in apps/runner/src/custom-tools.ts reading the agent's exemplar namespace (exemplarNamespace in packages/core/src/exemplar.ts) filtered by taskLabel with a small limit, positives and negatives separated; and a tool.principles.fetch returning promoted principles as scenario-scoped plus agent-wide union. Keep the injected block as the default and the tools as the precision path; register both in the tools registry so they remain shared, deterministic tools per doctrine.

name: Eval-gated self-improvement apply (frozen baseline case set)
mechanism: Any change to a prompt, skill, or routing config is intercepted before it takes effect and replayed against a frozen, version-pinned set of eval cases scored by a judge the agent cannot write to. The candidate must score at or above the recorded baseline or the change is refused, so self-improvement can only ratchet quality upward and never silently regress. The case set is grown from real production failures, and a 100% pass rate is treated as a signal the set is too easy, not that the system is done.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS has improve.ts (recurring-lesson mining -> guidance-block proposals -> operator apply queue) but the operator decides with zero objective evidence: no candidate-vs-baseline replay, no frozen case sets, no score attached to a proposal. A well-meaning approval can still ship a prompt that regresses the agent.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/eval/prompt-gate.ts: pure gatePromptCandidate(baselineScore, candidateScore, threshold) -> allow/refuse/insufficient_cases, plus case-set types {id, input, expected_traits, pinned_version}. Case files under packages/core/eval-cases/<agentKey>/*.json (operator-owned, never writable by any agent tool). An Inngest job replays cases through the candidate prompt in a sandboxed run and attaches {baseline, candidate, delta} to the improvement proposal row (extend migration for improvement_proposals.eval_result jsonb). Server-side apply endpoint refuses when delta < 0 unless the operator passes an explicit override flag; /proposals UI renders the delta badge.

name: Different-family quality judge with write-protected rubric and cross-judge bias neutralization
mechanism: Subjective artifact quality is scored on a separate axis from objective correctness by an LLM judge whose rubric lives in operator-owned code the evaluated agent can never see or edit, and whose model family deliberately differs from the worker's. When the candidate under evaluation is from the same family as the judge, a second judge from another family scores independently and the results are averaged, neutralizing same-family bias. The judge reads only the produced artifacts and returns a strict JSON verdict with per-dimension scores and a one-line rationale; the scoring machinery itself is proven against known-good reference artifacts (which must score ~100) before any ranking it produces is trusted.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's eval scorecard (packages/core/src/eval/scorecard.ts) is purely run-metric based (approval rate, failure rate) and the model-feedback loop derives scores from run highlights — there is no artifact-quality LLM judge at all, no fixed rubric, no family-separation discipline, and no reference-fixture verification of the scorer itself.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/eval/quality-judge.ts: RUBRICS map keyed by artifact type (email draft, report, code, landing page), buildJudgePrompt() producing a strict-JSON verdict schema, and pickJudges(workerModelSlug) that returns [T-critical Opus] normally but appends a non-Anthropic cross-judge slug when the worker is Anthropic, averaging overalls. Feed the resulting quality score into scorecard RunSample (new outputQuality field) and into router/model-feedback deriveOutcomeScore. Add eval/verify-scorers.ts with known-good and known-bad fixture artifacts that must score high/low respectively, wired into pnpm launch:check so a broken scorer fails the readiness oracle.

name: Judge-calibration loop against operator decisions
mechanism: Operator approve/edit/reject decisions are treated as ground-truth labels and periodically diffed against the automated judge's verdicts on the same items to measure agreement. When agreement drops below a threshold the system flags judge drift to the operator rather than silently continuing to trust the judge, and a small sample (1-2%) of judge-passed items is routed to the human anyway as a standing calibration check.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's exemplar.ts already harvests operator decisions as labels, but nothing compares those labels to any automated verdict — once a quality judge exists (or even against the existing scorecard's promote/demote calls), there is no drift detection and no calibration sampling; a mis-calibrated judge would degrade autonomy decisions invisibly.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/eval/judge-calibration.ts: pure computeAgreement(judgeVerdicts, operatorDecisions) -> {agreementRate, disagreements[], sampleSize}, plus shouldSampleForCalibration(runId, rate) for the 1-2% human-check draw. Scheduled Inngest job joins quality-judge verdicts with approvals rows per agent per window, emits a new Relay event judge.drift_detected below threshold, and surfaces agreement rate on the /performance route next to the scorecard.

name: Completion-evidence gate with judge-signed attestation and fresh-context adversarial audit
mechanism: Any 'done'-class signal is blocked at the tool-call hook until an evidence manifest exists, and the manifest is only trusted if a separate judge process has re-derived each verdict from the actual artifact bytes (re-hashing them) and signed the result with an HMAC secret only the judge holds — a self-asserted 'proven' gets overwritten by the judge's true verdict, and a missing signing secret fails closed. The audit itself runs in a fresh context given only the contract (never the builder's transcript), demands hard evidence per criterion, and loops fix-and-re-audit until a clean pass; a single pass is not the gate, the loop is.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS run success is whatever the runner reports — the scorecard consumes statuses, objective.ts retries on failure, but nothing verifies a claimed completion against artifacts, nothing signs verdicts, and the Phase 11 'verification-before-completion-v2' candidate exists only as quarantined prose on a branch with zero runtime enforcement. The building context grades its own homework.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/completion-evidence.ts: manifest types {criterion, evidenceRef, sha256, verdict, signedAt, signature}, verifyManifest(manifest, hmacKey) that re-computes signatures and fails closed on missing key, and deriveCriteria(jobInstructions) so criteria come from the job contract not the transcript. Runner: a Stop/PreToolUse check for completion-class tool names that blocks unless a verified manifest row exists for the run (new run_evidence table, RLS). Auditor runs as a sub-agent (apps/runner/src/sub-agent.ts) with a bundle deliberately excluding the run transcript. Non-cant-fail agents first; emit relay event completion.blocked_unproven.

name: Fleet-wide shadow-mode master switch with a fixed trust-ramp order
mechanism: One tenant-level shadow flag, default ON, forces every externally-visible or irreversible action to draft/propose regardless of what per-agent autonomy the ladder has earned; it is lifted only by an explicit recorded operator action after watching the fleet work. The ramp out of shadow follows a fixed, non-negotiable order (prove one low-blast-radius internal goal end-to-end under live gates on real data, then widen), and the climbing KPI that justifies each step is first-pass approval rate measured from the shadow drafts themselves.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS has per-agent autonomy (propose/execute_safe/execute_full), a scorecard-driven ladder, and a circuit breaker that ratchets down — but no single tenant-scoped override that wins over execute_full, no recorded 'operator lifted shadow in writing' moment, and no codified rollout order; a freshly onboarded tenant's fleet could reach execute_full agent-by-agent without any whole-fleet supervised period.
improvement_sketch: Add tenants.shadow_mode boolean default true (new migration) validated in tenant-config.ts. In packages/core/src/autonomy.ts, autonomyGate() takes tenantShadow and returns 'propose' for any irreversible/send-class tool while shadow is on, regardless of agent autonomy. Lift only via a dedicated API endpoint that records who/when and emits relay event tenant.shadow_lifted; /settings gets a confirmation-gated toggle. Document the fixed ramp order + first-pass-approval-rate KPI in docs (ties directly into the existing scorecard windows).

name: Layered send-clearance ledger (per-run and per-recipient caps, fail-closed reads, operator carve-out)
mechanism: Even after autonomy and approval clear, an outbound send must clear a stack of independent layers: shadow off, under a per-run send cap, under a per-recipient rolling-24h cap, an approval row bound to this specific run, an idempotency key, and a successful ledger write — and if the ledger cannot be read the send is denied (fail closed). The operator's own notification channel is explicitly carved out so safety machinery can never silence the heartbeat that tells the human what is happening. The design exists because a single runaway agent once fired 75 sends from one inbox.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS gates sends through autonomy + approvals, but an execute_full agent has no volume ceiling: no send ledger, no per-recipient cap, no idempotency key preventing duplicate sends on retry, and no run-bound approval check — exactly the 75-sends bug class the external runtime was hardened against.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/send-ledger.ts: pure clearSend({shadow, runSends, recipientSends24h, approvedRunId, runId, caps}) -> allow/deny+reason, isSendClassTool(name) matcher, and recipient normalization (hash email/phone). New send_ledger table (tenant_id, agent_id, run_id, recipient_hash, idempotency_key unique, ts) with RLS. Wire into buildPreToolUseHook in apps/runner/src/hooks.ts for send-class tools (same override path the injection guard uses); caps live in tenant config validated by the I-001 validators; deny emits relay event send.capped.

name: Secret-egress scan at the tool-call boundary
mechanism: Every file-write, commit, or outbound tool call has its full argument blob scanned against a bank of credential-shape patterns (provider key prefixes, cloud access keys, JWTs, private-key headers) with a placeholder-suppressor so templates and examples do not false-positive; any real match blocks the call before it executes. Separately, known vault key NAMES are blocked from being written into client-destined or external paths, so a missing credential becomes an escalation to the operator, never a substitution of the operator's own key. Argument keys are read defensively across common naming variants and the whole blob is scanned as fallback, so the gate fails safe rather than silently missing a field.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS encrypts secrets at rest (vault) and scrubs inbound content (injection-guard), but nothing inspects outbound tool arguments — an agent can currently paste a credential into a file write, a git commit, or an outbound message and no hook notices. The Phase 11 'secret-scan-veto' candidate is prose-only.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/security/secret-egress.ts mirroring injection-guard.ts's shape: SECRET_SHAPES pattern bank + PLACEHOLDER suppressor + scanToolArgs(toolName, argsJson) -> {blocked, category, span} with a window check around each match. Wire into buildPreToolUseHook (apps/runner/src/hooks.ts) as a deny-override exactly like the injection guard's override path; emit new relay event security.secret_egress_blocked. Vault key-name list sourced from the vault package so it stays in sync. Offline test suite with real-shaped fakes and placeholder negatives.

name: Tenant doctrine layer (SOUL-style identity injected into every run, hooks framed as the floor)
mechanism: A single operator-owned doctrine document — who the agent org is, the mission and north-star metric, voice rules, and the hard gates restated as identity ('these are bright lines drawn from real incidents') — follows every agent into every session, layered above the per-agent persona. The load-bearing framing is that code-enforced hooks are the floor, not the plan: the model is told to never get near the line, which makes the prompt layer and the hook layer reinforce each other instead of the prompt treating gates as obstacles. Business facts live in a separate injected file, and procedures live in skills, keeping the doctrine short and stable.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS composes bundles from per-agent persona + versioned prompt + skills + guidance block, but has no shared tenant-level identity/doctrine layer — each agent's prompt restates (or omits) mission, voice, and safety posture independently, so fleet-wide values drift agent by agent and nothing tells every agent that the hooks are a floor it should stay far away from.
improvement_sketch: Add a doctrine document type: either tenants.doctrine_md text column or a reserved documents row of type 'doctrine' per tenant (small migration). In packages/core/src/bundle.ts, compose the doctrine block first in the system prompt, above persona and the improve.ts guidance block; keep it operator-editable only (no agent tool can write it — enforce with the same no-surface-in-types pattern exemplar.ts uses). Seed a starter doctrine for Acqu covering mission, voice rules, and the gates-as-floor framing; render/edit on a /settings doctrine panel.

name: Intent lock — sealed scope contract with typed drift detection
mechanism: At the moment intake is approved, the system writes an immutable record of the goal text plus the sorted deliverables list, and stores a hash computed over a canonicalized JSON form of those two fields. Before and after every subsequent phase, a verifier re-derives goal+deliverables from the current live spec, recomputes the hash, and compares. Mismatches are classified into typed errors: deliverables added means scope-expanded, deliverables dropped means scope-reduced, and identical deliverable sets with different goal wording means interpretation drift (treated as expansion). The build halts on any drift rather than silently absorbing it.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS has nothing that pins original intent. Onboarding interview goals, architect blueprints, and objective descriptions are all mutable DB rows; improve.ts mutates prompts (with operator queue) and reflexion retries re-read the objective row each attempt, so a mid-flight edit to an objective or blueprint silently changes what 'success' means. The critic quorum reviews actions, not scope; overlap.ts checks intra-blueprint collisions, not blueprint-vs-interview fidelity.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/intent-lock.ts: sealIntent(tenantId, {goal, deliverables[]}) canonicalizes (trim, sort, stable-key JSON) and stores a SHA-256 digest in a new intent_locks table (append-only, tenant-scoped). verifyIntent(tenantId, currentSpec) returns {ok} | {drift: 'expanded'|'reduced'|'goal_mutated', diff}. Wire three call sites: (1) provision.ts seals at blueprint approval and verifies before seeding; (2) objective.ts records a per-objective seal of title+description at creation and decideReflexion() abandons with a 'scope_drifted' rationale if the row changed between attempts; (3) architect re-proposals verify against the sealed interview and emit a Relay event architect.scope_drift for the operator queue instead of hard-failing.

name: Interrogation-before-provisioning — confidence-gated clarify rounds with preview-before-write
mechanism: After automatic extraction of a spec from raw intake, each extracted field carries a confidence score. A bounded question loop (max 2 rounds, max 4 questions per round) targets only low-confidence or missing fields, always includes a rendered plain-text preview of the full interpreted spec as one selectable option ('show me what you extracted'), and merges answers back into the spec. Answers themselves can introduce new gaps (e.g. choosing an expanded scope option adds a credentials question), which is what triggers round 2. If required fields remain unresolved after round 2, intake fails closed with a typed error rather than proceeding on guesses; every answer round is persisted atomically for audit.
gap_vs_agentos: onboarding.ts only does shape validation (min lengths, slug regex, CRA keyword gate) then composes the architect prompt directly. There is no confidence scoring on interpreted fields, no targeted clarification loop, no 'here is what I understood' preview before the architect runs, and no fail-closed path for ambiguous intake — a vague interview flows straight into blueprint generation and burns an LLM round on bad input.
improvement_sketch: Extend packages/core/src/onboarding.ts (or new onboarding-interrogate.ts): add ExtractedField<T> = {value, confidence, source}; interrogationQuestions(iv) returns up to 4 typed question objects biased to confidence < 0.9 (budget sanity band, connector scope toggle, goal-restatement confirm), each with a renderTextPreview(iv) option showing company/goals/budget/proposed-gate summary; mergeAnswers(iv, answers) recomputes pending gaps; after 2 rounds throw IncompleteOnboardingError. Persist rounds in an onboarding_answers JSONB column. The control-plane onboarding UI (apps/control-plane) renders the question batches; planOnboardingSteps() gains an 'interrogate' step between validate_interview and architect_propose.

name: Fingerprint-keyed idempotency for mutating tools + check-before-create
mechanism: Every external side effect is wrapped in a decorator that computes a SHA-256 fingerprint over (service, operation, canonicalized args) — with a declared exclude-list so volatile fields like timestamps don't bust the cache — and stores the call result keyed by that fingerprint. Re-issuing the identical call after a crash or retry returns the cached result instead of duplicating the external write. This is complemented by check-before-create helpers: before creating a remote resource, look up whether the spec already records its ID and verify it still exists upstream; and stage-complete markers that let a rerun skip finished stages entirely.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS's only idempotency is run-claim (claim.ts) and duplicate terminal-status posts (lifecycle.ts). The mutating tools in apps/runner/src/lead-pipeline-tools.ts and custom-tools.ts (CRM writes, lead updates, sends) have no result cache — and reflexion (objective.ts) deliberately re-queues whole runs on failure, so attempt N+1 can re-execute attempt N's already-committed external writes: duplicate CRM rows, duplicate outreach. That is the exact hazard this pattern exists for.
improvement_sketch: New apps/runner/src/idempotency.ts: withIdempotency(toolKey, handler, {excludeFields}) wraps a CustomToolHandler; fingerprint = sha256(canonicalJSON({tenantId, toolKey, filteredInput})); results persist in a new tool_call_cache table (tenant_id, tool_key, fingerprint PK, result JSONB, run_id, created_at) so the cache survives runner restarts and is visible cross-attempt within an objective chain. Apply to the mutating subset of the tool catalog (writes to Close, lead upserts, sends); read-only tools skip it. Add a per-tool TTL/scope knob (per-objective vs per-tenant) and emit a Relay event tool.idempotent_replay on cache hits so operators see suppressed duplicates.

name: Post-provision fleet verifier — evidence-typed checks with ship/hold/rebuild verdict
mechanism: After a build declares itself complete, a read-only verifier opens the real artifacts (never mutates them) and runs a per-track checklist where every check returns a status plus a human-readable evidence string (e.g. 'client name found in output', 'output contains placeholder tokens', 'cost exceeded 20% of deal value'). Checks include content validity (does the artifact actually mention the client?), placeholder detection (TBD/TODO in first record), plaintext-credential scanning, and cost-vs-value ratio. Results aggregate into a structured verdict — ship, hold-for-review, or rebuild-stage — written atomically as a machine-readable result file; checks that need a human are explicitly marked deferred rather than skipped.
gap_vs_agentos: provision.ts (provisionClientTenant) has zero verification after seeding — no check that seeded agents resolve to valid models, that connector bindings reach their MCPs, that RLS holds for the new tenant, or that a canary run succeeds. AgentOS's verification is per-run (verificationPassed on attempts) and repo-level (pnpm launch:check); nothing verifies a freshly provisioned FLEET end-to-end, and nothing produces per-check evidence + a graded recommendation for the operator queue.
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/provision-verify.ts: verifyProvisionedFleet(tenantId, deps) runs read-only checks each returning {status: 'PASS'|'FAIL'|'WARN'|'deferred_to_operator', evidence: string}: every blueprint agent exists + resolveModel() succeeds; T-critical agents resolved to Opus; each bound MCP present in registry; RLS spot-check via tool-rls-test returns zero cross-tenant rows; budget caps configured; one T-cheap canary dispatch completes. Aggregate to {verified, checks, issues, recommendation: 'ship'|'hold_for_review'|'reprovision'} persisted on the tenant row and emitted as Relay event provision.verified for the control-plane operator surface. planOnboardingSteps() gains a terminal 'verify_fleet' step.

name: Per-agent runaway-spend breaker (share-of-budget, not just total)
mechanism: Alongside the total cost ceiling, the budget layer aggregates spend per agent across all phases and trips a distinct typed error when any single agent's cumulative spend crosses a fixed share of the TOTAL ceiling (20% in the source design) — deliberately measured against the full ceiling, not remaining budget, so the threshold doesn't shrink as the build progresses. The runaway error subclasses the generic budget-exceeded error so existing handlers catch it transparently, while a dedicated notification names the specific agent for triage.
gap_vs_agentos: budget/tracker.ts does per-run reserve/commit and tenant-cap.ts enforces a tenant monthly ceiling, but nothing attributes spend concentration to a single agent. One misbehaving agent making many individually-cheap runs burns the whole tenant cap with no early signal and no attribution; the anomaly breaker watches failure streaks, not cost concentration.
improvement_sketch: Extend packages/core/src/budget/: new runaway.ts with checkRunawayAgent(tenantId, window): sums committed spend per agent_id over the current cap window (query the same ledger tenant-cap reads), and when any agent >= runawayPct (default 0.2, tenant-configurable via tenant-config validators) of the tenant cap, returns a typed RunawayAgentBreach {agentId, spend, capUsd, pct}. Wire it into the same evaluation cadence as eval/circuit-breaker.ts: a breach feeds the autonomy ladder (demote to propose) and emits Relay event budget.runaway_agent. S-sized because the ledger and cap plumbing already exist.

name: Structured lesson write-back to shared knowledge on objective close
mechanism: When a build finishes (success or abandonment), a non-LLM templated post-mortem document is generated from data already on hand: what worked (completed steps), what failed (recorded errors), open questions (pulled from state docs), and a numbers table (phases run, errors, elapsed, cost). The doc is written to a lessons directory and a one-line pointer is idempotently inserted at the top of a central index under a known heading — newest first, skipped if already present — so future builds discover prior lessons without scanning. Template-based generation means write-back can never fail on LLM flakiness and costs nothing.
gap_vs_agentos: memory.ts composes episodes + heuristic lessons but namespaces them PER AGENT (episodeNamespace(agentId)) — agent B never learns from agent A's failure. improve.ts turns lessons into prompt proposals for the same agent. There is no cross-agent, tenant-level post-mortem artifact when an objective completes/abandons, and nothing indexes outcomes into the shared pgvector store (knowledge.ts indexDocument exists but is never fed by the objective loop).
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/lesson-writeback.ts: composeObjectiveLesson(objective, attempts[], costSummary) builds a deterministic markdown doc (worked/failed/open-questions/numbers sections) from AttemptOutcome rows and budget ledger data — no LLM call. On decideReflexion() returning 'complete' or 'abandon', the lifecycle sink calls indexDocument(tenantId, doc, {namespace: 'lessons', source: objectiveId}) so ALL agents in the tenant retrieve it via the existing retrieve() path; formatPriorLearnings() in the runner bundle gains a second section for tenant-level lessons alongside agent episodes. Idempotent on objectiveId so a re-fired sink doesn't double-index.

name: Transient/hard-stop error taxonomy + narrow re-emit retry in the runner
mechanism: The agent runner classifies every exception by substring taxonomy into transient (overload, rate limit, 5xx, timeout — retry in-place with differentiated backoff: long fixed sleep for rate limits, exponential otherwise) versus hard-stop (billing, auth, quota, permission — raise immediately, never retry, since retrying burns money on an unfixable condition). Separately, when an agent completes but its expected structured output artifact is missing, the runner does ONE cheap targeted retry with a terse re-emit instruction ('write only the expected file, valid JSON, do not narrate') instead of failing the whole run and paying for a full re-execution.
gap_vs_agentos: The runner (apps/runner/src) has no error taxonomy — grep shows retry logic only in lease-integration (retryAfterMs for lease conflicts). A rate-limit blip and an invalid API key both fail the run identically, and reflexion then re-queues a FULL new attempt (full context re-send, full cost) for what a 75-second in-run backoff or a one-line re-emit prompt would have fixed; a billing error can burn all 3 reflexion attempts pointlessly.
improvement_sketch: New apps/runner/src/error-taxonomy.ts: classifyError(err) → 'transient' | 'hard_stop' | 'unknown' via fragment lists (rate_limit/overloaded/5xx/timeout vs billing/auth/quota/permission). execute.ts wraps the SDK query loop: transient → in-run backoff (fixed 60-90s for rate limits, 2^n otherwise, max 2 in-run retries) before surfacing failure; hard_stop → fail the run with a status that objective.ts's decideReflexion treats as immediate 'abandon' (new AttemptOutcome flag hardStop: true) so reflexion budget isn't burned. Add a missing-artifact micro-retry where the runner expects structured output (dispatch-contract results): one follow-up turn with a minimal re-emit instruction before marking the run failed.

name: Deterministic rescue triage — state inference to patch/rebuild/abandon with named rules
mechanism: For a project in an unknown or broken state, a pure rule-based classifier (explicitly no LLM, for observability) takes an inferred state snapshot plus the operator's declared intent and walks a fixed precedence chain: hard red flags (committed credentials, corrupted spec, schema violation) → abandon/escalate; no substantive content → rebuild; declared intent diverging from inferred track → rebuild (a patch can't reconcile drift); mostly-complete state with only soft flags → patch with high confidence; everything else → patch with LOW confidence, explicitly surfaced for operator review. The first entry of every verdict's reasons list is always the machine-searchable rule ID that fired, and each verdict carries a confidence number with a documented review threshold.
gap_vs_agentos: AgentOS has no triage path for a half-provisioned or interrupted tenant: if onboarding dies mid-seed or an operator abandons a blueprint, there is no state inferrer, no deterministic resume/reseed/escalate verdict — the operator eyeballs tables. The 'rule_fired first in reasons, confidence attached, low-confidence surfaces to human' observability convention also doesn't exist in AgentOS's decision functions (decideReflexion returns prose rationale only).
improvement_sketch: New packages/core/src/rescue.ts: inferTenantState(tenantId, db) → {hasBlueprint, approvedBlueprint, seededAgentCount, expectedAgentCount, redFlags[]} where hard flags include t_critical_model_drift, rls_probe_failed, vault_secret_in_prompt; classifyRescue(state, declaredIntent) → {verdict: 'resume'|'reprovision'|'escalate', reasons: ['rule_fired=R-...', ...], confidence}. Verdicts under 0.6 confidence always route to the operator queue. Wire as a control-plane 'Fix this tenant' action and as a pre-flight in provisionClientTenant() when a tenant row already exists. Secondary: adopt the rule_fired-first reasons convention in decideReflexion and evaluateCircuitBreaker for log-searchable decisions.
